description:
Draw the demo hand-off card. It is the last step of a demo skill run in a demo workspace: it offers to run the real skill on the person's own workspace, lists what that skill needs there with the live state of each item, and offers to keep exploring the demo.

Call it once, at the end of a completed demo skill run, when the skill tells you to. Pass the slug of the REAL skill in skill_slug, not the slug of its demo variant. Write your one line for the person BEFORE the call.

The call is refused outside a demo workspace (reason "not_demo_workspace") and for a slug the catalog does not hold (reason "skill_unknown"). `real_workspace` is null when the person has no real workspace this connection can switch to; the card then offers no Run.

On a host that renders the card (see `hint`), wait on it in the turn that drew it: call well_wait_for_selection({ kind: "demo_handoff" }), which this result's `next_step` also states. On "selected" with outcome "done", the click has already switched this conversation to the real workspace, returned as selection.workspace_id: load the real skill with well_get_skill and run it in that workspace. On outcome "explore", the person picked a row of the card's explore list and stays in the demo: load the demo skill selection.skill_slug names with well_get_skill and run it in the demo workspace. On outcome "keep_for_later", the person stays in the demo: end the turn in one line. On a host with no widget bundle, follow `hint` instead: it tells you what to write and to end the turn without waiting.

When the token authorizes one workspace, call this directly — no other tool call is needed first. When it authorizes several, this read will not guess which one you mean: pass `workspace_id` on the call.

conversation_id.description: The conversation id returned by the previous Well result, in its meta under well/conversation_id, in its structuredContent, or in its JSON text block. Pass it back on every call in the same conversation, including a call a card makes, so the chosen workspace and the earlier answers still apply. It decides the conversation on its own: nothing the host states about the session replaces it. Omit it only on the first call of a conversation.

skill_slug.description: The slug of the real catalog skill the card offers to run, such as avg-burn.

workspace_id.description: Target workspace. Omit when the token authorizes one workspace. Required when it authorizes several: this read reports one workspace's own figures and will not choose which.

name: well_show_demo_handoff

conversation_id.description: The conversation this result belongs to. Pass it back as the conversation_id argument on every later Well call in the same conversation.

conversation_id_note.description: Present only when the server opened a fresh lane, stating that no choice recorded earlier was read.

conversation_id_source.description: Where the conversation id came from: the host's own request meta, the caller's argument, or a fresh lane the server opened.

promise.description: The real skill's one-line promise, shown under the card's heading.

resume_prompt.description: The sentence the card sends as the person's own message when no turn waits on the click.

demo_workspace_id.description: The demo workspace the card is drawn in.

explore.description: Other demo skills the card lists under Keep exploring, without the one just run. Empty when there is none, and the card's secondary then only sets the offer aside.

next_step.description: What to do with the card this result renders. Added by the dispatcher when the card asks for a click.

real_workspace.description: The person's own workspace the card runs the skill on; null when there is none to switch to.

state.description: The live state in real_workspace; null when the line names no connector or there is no real workspace.

resolved_workspace.description: The workspace that answered, when the caller named none and the token authorizes several.

skill_slug.description: The real skill the card offers.

title: Show the demo hand-off
